When the `if` branch ends with `return`, the code after the `if` only runs if the condition was false. An `else` around that code adds a level of indentation and says nothing new.

`--fix` removes the `else` and moves its content out of the block, unless a name declared in the block would clash with one outside it.

{/* Generated by src/codegen/lint-rule-docs.ts. Do not edit this section. */}

## Configure

Off by default. To turn it on:

```toml bunfig.toml
[lint.rules]
"no-else-return" = "error" # or "warn"
```

Every option, set to its default:

```toml bunfig.toml
[lint.rules]
"no-else-return" = ["error", {
  allowElseIf = true,
}]
```

{/* End of the generated section. */}

## Examples

Reported:

{/* bad */}
```js
function label(user) {
  if (user.admin) {
    return "Admin";
  } else {
    return "Member";
  }
}
```

Not reported:

{/* good */}
```js
function label(user) {
  if (user.admin) {
    return "Admin";
  }
  return "Member";
}
```

## Options

| Option | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `allowElseIf` | `true` | Allow `else if` after a branch that returns. |

By default an `else if` is fine:

{/* good */}
```js
function label(user) {
  if (user.admin) {
    return "Admin";
  } else if (user.guest) {
    return "Guest";
  }
  return "Member";
}
```

The last `else` of a chain is still reported if every branch before it returns:

{/* bad */}
```js
function label(user) {
  if (user.admin) {
    return "Admin";
  } else if (user.guest) {
    return "Guest";
  } else {
    return "Member";
  }
}
```

With `allowElseIf: false`, the `else if` is reported too:

{/* bad {"options": [{"allowElseIf": false}]} */}
```js
function label(user) {
  if (user.admin) {
    return "Admin";
  } else if (user.guest) {
    return "Guest";
  }
  return "Member";
}
```
